newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki falls in lively trade on Wall St jitters.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki falls in lively trade on Wall St jitters.

text.p: Shares fell on Thursday as Wall Street remained wary after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on Wednesday, brokers said.

The market opened weak, attempted a recovery at noon but fell again after strong U.S. durable goods data dragged long U.S. Treasuries lower, with the HEX general index closing 0.32 percent lower at 2,920.00 points.
Derivatives expiry boosted volume to 966 million markka with 34 percent in bourse engine Nokia which fell 1.50 markka to 309.00.
"Buyers have not disappeared, but they will stay on hold until next week," he said, adding that options and futures expiry and Wall Street's jitters kept investors sidelined.
"We will see the real market next week," said another.
Oil and energy group Neste hit a new 147.40 all-time high intra-session but turned lower in the afternoon to close down 2.50 at 144.50 markka ahead of its 1996 report due on Friday.
Forestries bucked the trend on the back of overnight gains in U.S. paper stocks and the sub-index rose 0.25 percent. The largest foresty industry group UPM-Kymmene closed flat at 106.00.
Construction group Polar fell 0.15 to 7.90 on a disappointing 1996 loss, and beverage group Hartwall fell 1.00 to 235.00 after announcing a lower-than expected dividend.
Aspoyhtyma also fell after its dividend announcement, ending down 3.50 markka at 220.00.
